Troyitske Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Odessa Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Troitske's Jewish population numbered 587 (19 percent) in 1897; under Soviet rule in the 1920s, the community maintained a Jewish library and club, though the population had fallen to 220 by 1939. Nazi troops occupied the town on August 8, 1941, and executed 74 Jews on September 27 of that year. This cemetery, marked on a Russian map from 1917, was presumably ruined during or shortly after WWII; a local resident recalled that the gravestones were already broken by the 1950s.
